The way out is clear. I swept it while we talked. I always sweep while I talk. Goodbye.
Leave a footprint or two at the door, if you like. I'll leave them. Just this once.
Ash follows. Mind it doesn't follow you all the way home.
I'll leave your last print where it is. It's the best one yet. Good luck.
The ash will remember you a little longer than I will. That's not an insult. It's just how I'm made.
Back to the broom. A path out here doesn't sweep itself. Well, it does, in time. But in time is a long way off.
Safe path. Dry ash. A quiet pillar. That's the whole of my blessing, and I'm told it's a good one.
Goodbye. If you meet a magma cube on the way, it isn't my fault. It did leave from here.
Goodbye. I'll sweep where you stood. That's not an insult. It's how a sweeper says a place was visited.
I'll keep the sky for you. If anything is hunting your path, I'll... well. I'll know. Go on.
There's a clear stretch to the east and a Weft net in the west gap. East, then.
I'll lose you in the smoke in three breaths. Wave if you want me to know you're still there.
Go. And if you hear a high whistle behind you, don't turn. That's me, giving the all-clear.
I'll watch your side of the sky until you're out of it, and then the other side, because it's the side you came from.
If the smoke closes round you out there, stop and breathe. I've never seen it keep anyone. It only makes them think so.
Safe crossing. I'm on this pillar a long while yet. If I see you again I'll nod. If I don't, I won't mention it.
The mourners are drifting east. Go west for now. They aren't looking for you, but they're sad enough to bump into you.
Don't dawdle. A traveller who dawdles in the delta is a story I'd rather not watch the end of.
Goodbye. I'm going back to counting. It's fourteen. Last time it was thirteen. Don't ask.
Bye! I'll practise floating until you're back, and then I'll show you. It'll be amazing. Or I'll fall. Both are entertaining.
Bye bye bye! Come back before the pool dries up! It never does, but come back anyway.
Wait! Take this pebble. It hums, but it stops if you're sad, so check it sometimes. All right, bye.
Go quietly so the big ghasts don't look! They always look at loud people. I think they like loud people, which is the problem.
Will you come back? I'll save the good smoke on the gallery for you. I won't let anyone else sit in it.
I'll wave till I can't see you, and then I'll wave a bit more in case you can see me. You might. Goodbye!
Come back soon. Come back soonest. I'll be the one on the vine with the silly grin. Don't tell me it's silly.
Bye! I'll wait here for Mama. If she asks, I wasn't talking to an outsider. I was talking to a rock that moves.
Bye! I'm going to tell {neighbour} everything you said. Not all of it. The good parts. And the funny parts. And the part I made up.
Don't worry about me crying. I haven't started. I'm not sad. I'm just a bit hollow where you were.
Goodbye. I'll count to a hundred and then I'll miss you. Or a bit before. I get impatient.
Papa says the Nether is dangerous. It's less dangerous with you in it. Or more? I forgot which. Bye!
Come back and teach me a new game! Not hide-and-seek, I'm too good at hide-and-seek. Something with a ball. Or a vine. Or both.
Right now I'm at 'worried'. By the time you're back I'll be at 'amazing'. Bye!
If a Piglin chases you, float! Oh. You can't. Then run very quietly. That's a thing.
All right, bye. I'm going to pretend you didn't leave. I'll talk to the air where you were. It's a good game.
I'll tell the Ashbells you said goodbye. They'll ring. That's how they say it back. Bye!
Goodbye! Say my name three times in the smoke and I'll know. That's a Ghastkin trick. It isn't true, but it works.
I'm leaving first! No, you. No, me. Go on, you first, I'll stay. We'll never finish. That's how I know we're friends.
Bye! If you get lost, find a pillar and wait. Pillars are good at being found.
Goodbye, stranger in the smoke. I don't mean it as a name, only a title. It's what we call everyone before we've decided.
Go on. I'll pretend I didn't enjoy that. It's easier on my reputation.
Mind your step on the way. The delta doesn't know you yet, and it isn't gentle with the unknown.
Thank you for keeping quiet. You've no idea what a gift that is. Or you do. Goodbye.
I won't wave. A wave would carry. Consider yourself waved at, silently, in my head.
Come again, soft-foot. You've a way of leaving that makes the place feel rested. Odd, but there it is.
I've decided not to worry about you. I'll be worrying for a few moments in the corner, privately.
I liked that, you know. Talking. It isn't usually this easy with someone who stands so very upright. Mostly.
Take a candle's worth of the Eave with you. It's invisible, but I can see it. Go well.
Goodbye. I'll tell {neighbour} you were kind. It will annoy them. They'd have bet you wouldn't be.
I'll leave my pod door on the latch. It isn't an invitation, it's a habit. All right, it's an invitation.
I'll leave a candle on the rail where you stood. It isn't a message. It's only a habit I've picked up from watching you leave.
Go with half my name. I'm keeping the other half in case you forget to return. Safe path, friend.
Whatever happens out there, send me nothing. I'll know. I always know. It's both our gift and our problem.
You're leaving. I've just remembered the thing I wanted to tell you. It'll keep. Most things do, with a little salt.
Go, but not too far. I've made a habit of you, and habits are the hardest names to cry away.
When you're gone I'll stay exactly as I am, with one small space beside me. Don't let anything else fill it.
I'm not going to say it's goodbye. We don't have goodbyes at our level. We have: until the smoke thins. Until the smoke thins.
If the ghasts ask, I'll tell them you're mine. They'll keep off. Ghasts respect a claim. Go, go. Come back.
I keep your name where I keep the ones I'll never cry away. There's only one other in there. Goodbye, friend.
Back to the pods, then. Mind the third rung, it's rotten. I'd mend it, but then nobody would know to mind it.
Goodbye from {village}. The vines will see you off. They'll pretend not to, but they'll rustle when you've gone.
The Eave sees you out. The pillars lean a little, I think. No, that's only me. Go gently.
Go well. If you meet any of ours on the way, say you saw {name} and I was well. They worry.
The delta is wide and I'm in it somewhere. If we meet again it will be by luck, and I'll try to be pleased.
I'll stay a while with the pillar. It's good company, and it has never once left before I did.
Go on. The ash will fill in your steps and the delta will pretend you were never here. I won't.
I'm headed the other way. A pity. We'd have made quiet companions. Goodbye.
I'll draw my veil down and hum you out of hearing. That's the courtesy of the veiled.
One bead for this meeting. It will clink with the rest. Goodbye.
I'll think of you whenever the circlet catches the light. It does that when I'm not looking. I'm looking now.
I'll pull the hood forward and watch you go from inside it. It makes a departure more dramatic. Goodbye.
My cape will be at the door when you come back. I'll be in it. Or not. The cape is the dependable one.
Hood up, head down, heart somewhere on the ladder. Goodbye. The ladder is an old joke.
Mind where you point that. And thank you for not pointing it here.
Mind the bucket. Carry it somewhere you can pour it out softly.
Use that tear well. Someone cried it very properly, whoever they were. They'd be glad it has gone to a friend.

farewell: Goodbye. Take the quiet with you, if there's any left in your pockets.
Go safely. May the sky above you stay clear, even if the ground doesn't.
Go on, then. The ash is already thinking of covering your steps.
Goodbye for now. The smoke will keep your place.
Off you go. I'll tell the pillars you said goodbye. They'll pass it along, eventually.

refuse.text: *drifts up out of reach, very fast, saying nothing at all*
No. You hurt me. I'm going up where your hands can't reach. Don't follow. You can't, but don't.
I won't cry over this. Nobody died. But I won't talk to you, either.
*one soft falling note, and then only the chains creaking*
You crept up quietly so you could do that? Clever. I'll remember it. From us, that's the worst thing there is to hear.
You hit me! The grown-ups said outsiders do that. I didn't believe them. *floats away up the vines*
*hides behind the weeping vines, eyes very wide, saying nothing*
*the rack hums sharply, and the Tearkeeper pulls a cloth over the vials as if to hide them from you*
I have healed worse than you. I'll not heal you. Not for a long while. That isn't a threat. It's a vial I've closed.
You struck someone who carries tears for the wounded. Think about that, once, slowly. I'll wait over here, high up.
Don't ask me for a drop. I'd have to choose what you forget, and I'm too hurt to choose gently. So I won't choose at all.
*a single note drops, flat, and does not resolve*
The Song has no verse for this. I'd have to invent one, and I don't want to. Leave me to the quiet.
You struck me in the middle of a rest. The rest is the one place nobody gets hurt. Go away. Carefully.
No verse. No humming. No words. Only air. That is what you've earned.
*the needle stops mid-stitch, and the Mender turns away, taking the work high up out of reach*
I can mend a cape, a rope, a veil. I can't mend this, and I won't try with you in reach. Go.
You've torn something in the quiet between us. I'll mend it. Alone. Later. Go.
I'm not talking while there's a fist near my work. Go and let your hands remember what they're for.
*the broom stops. The Ashsweeper drifts up out of reach and sweeps nothing, very slowly*
I'll sweep your footprints out when you've gone. All of them. You'll leave no mark here. It's the kindest thing I can think of.
I sweep up what others leave. I won't sweep this away. It stays where you put it. Go.
I have swept a hundred galleries clean and never once felt dirty until now. Go.
I saw it coming and I didn't call the alarm. That's on me. Next time I'll call it. Go.
*goes up the vines fast and settles on the highest perch, watching you with studied calm*
I watch the sky for dangers. I'd never thought to watch the ground. Lesson learned. Please go.
Hit a watcher and the whole Eave hears. Good, because I'm not going to say it again. I'll point, and they'll understand.
Ow! You hit me! Papa said outsiders do that and I said no, and now I'm wrong, and I hate being wrong. *floats behind a pillar*
I'm not talking to you. I'm not. I'm counting the vines. One, two, three. Go away.
*sniffs, holds very still, and does not cry, because it hasn't learned how*
That hurt. It hurt and I don't know where to put it. Go away so I can find a place.
You were my friend and then you were a hitter. I'm too small to be both at once. Go away, please.
I'm telling Mama. And the Songwarden. And the Ashbells. They'll ring at you and it will be so embarrassing.
*floats very high and very fast, and hides in the dark under a pod*
No! I don't like you. Maybe later. Maybe not. Don't follow me, I'm faster upward.
I knew it. The grown ones told me. I'm not mad, I'm only right. It's terrible.
Go away, go away, go away. Three times. That's how you say it so the basalt hears.
Outsiders hit. I was told so, and I hoped it was only a story. Please leave. I'll go back to hoping.
I won't talk. Not because I'm angry, but because I'm very busy being frightened at a polite distance.
You and I have exchanged exactly one thing, and it was a blow. I'll wait for a better thing.
*a hand-span of silence, and then the Ghastkin is simply further away than before*
I thought you were different. I'm sorry, I did. It's a lesson, and I'm not fond of lessons. Go.
We were getting on so well. Now I'm up here and you're down there. How tidy. How tiring.
Don't speak. If you speak I'll answer, and I'm not ready to be kind. Give me a little while.
That hurt more than it should have. That's how I know I'd let you close. Please let me close it again.
I'll forgive you. I'm built for it. But not while my arm still remembers. Come back when the smoke has settled.
I looked for a reason and there wasn't one. That's the worst sort. Stay away until you've found me one.
You're a friend, so I'll say it plain: I'm hurt, and I don't want to look at you while it's still new.
Lantern-kin. Was it by accident? Please say it was by accident. ... No, don't say anything. Not yet.
I don't want to cry for this. It isn't a death. But it's near enough to the edge of one that I'm standing very still.
I'll keep your name. I'll keep the other things I know of you. But I'll keep them somewhere I can't see, for now.
You. Of all of them. ... No. I won't finish that. If I finish it, I'll have to feel it. Go.
I would have cried for you. Properly, all the way. Now I'm standing here not crying, and it's the strangest thing I've done.
There was a space in my chest the shape of you, and it just closed. I'd rather it hadn't. Give it time.
I won't swell. I won't forget. It's a very small grief, the size of one blow. Let me do it properly and alone.
Friend. Please step back. Not forever. Only far enough that I can't smell the iron on you.
Not here. Not in the Eave. We don't strike one another under these pillars, and we don't let it be done to us. Go outside.
{village} is watching. The vines have gone stiff. That's as close to a shout as they get.
Nobody's out here to see. That's the worst of it. Just us, and the ash, and the thing you did.
I came out into the delta to be left alone, and you, of all things, found me. *drifts up and out of the smoke's reach*
*the veil falls across the face, and the circlet's beads go still, one by one*
I'd lift my veil to look at you properly, but I don't want to see. Not yet.
*the hood goes up and the cape wraps close, until the whole Ghastkin is a closed door*
I'm keeping my hood up. It's the only wall I own. Please respect it.

refuse: *goes still, and then simply isn't within reach any more*
I'm not angry. I'm a bit sore, and the sore needs quiet. Give it some.
Quietly, now. Go quietly. Don't make me say it twice.
The smoke will settle. So will I. Not while you're standing there.
Nothing. I'm saying nothing. Look how well I'm saying it.
